ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover every ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) at or above 25%, all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, senior managers, attorneys-in-fact, and bank account operatives against the People's Bank of China PEP and financial intelligence lists, the State Administration for Market Regulation disqualified-person database, Ministry of Public Security wanted and felony status lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists for USD clearing, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, and Taiwan-specific court, bankruptcy, and regulatory disqualification records. The screening must be run using full legal name, aliases, Chinese character variants, English transliterations, passport or Taiwan ID numbers, nationality, citizenship, and residential address. Each screening hit requires enhanced due diligence with independent source-of-funds evidence, media and adverse news search, corporate relationship chart verification, and approval by a qualified compliance officer before incorporation may proceed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Reservation and Independent Name Declaration System, administered by the local State Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform and provincial market registration portals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE must adopt a mandatory simplified-Chinese company name. The four-tier statutory naming structure is: administrative division plus distinctive brand token plus industry description plus organizational form, for example 'Shanghai [Brand] Digital Game Art Design Co., Ltd.' The distinctive token may be a Chinese, pinyin, or English-derived brand but must be in simplified Chinese characters in the registered name; English names are auxiliary and must be declared to the AMR where legally required. Phonetic transliteration is permitted for the distinctive token but must not mislead as to state affiliation, public authority, licensed industry, or prohibited business scope.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, obtain the written AMR rejection notice with the specific legal basis, amend and re-submit the name through the same online portal within the 30-day reservation window. If the rejection rests on substantive grounds, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the next-higher AMR within 60 days from the date of receipt of the written decision, or initiate an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months. Preserve all system submission timestamps, name declaration codes, rejection screenshots, and correspondence with the local AMR documentation office to support the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox alone is not permissible for a China WFOE. PRC Company Law requires the registered address to be the principal place of actual business operation, and the local AMR, tax bureau, and PBOC-supervised banks will reject a non-operative address. For an asset-light 3D game art outsourcing business, a fully leased serviced office with a legal workspace, on-site personnel, and utility and internet infrastructure can satisfy the commercial-substance tests; a stand-alone mail-forwarding address without a physical lease or employees is high-risk and will trigger regulatory refusal, bank account denial, or suspected shell-company classification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Baseline likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by municipal tax or AMR authorities in the first 12 months is approximately 10% to 15%; the risk rises to 40% to 60% if the company applies for export VAT refunds, submits abnormal zero-revenue returns, receives large PayPal or wire transfers with no matching payroll, operates from a virtual office, or shows mismatched addresses among SAMR, tax, and bank filings. Mandatory inspection checklist: original lease contract and property ownership certificate; rental payment receipts; on-site signage; employee attendance and payroll records; utility, water, internet, and telephone invoices; computer hardware and licensed software for 3D art production; a network IP address trail consistent with the claimed office; and the WFOE business license and tax registration certificate displayed at the physical premises. Failure to allow entry or the discovery of a sealed non-operational office will be treated as proof that the company lacks commercial substance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online through the National Unified Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) platform linked from the STA official portal www.chinatax.gov.cn and administered by the provincial/municipal competent tax authorities
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign parent establishing a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE): (1) register the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation and obtain the Business License carrying the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory taxpayer identification number for all tax purposes; (2) tax registration is completed automatically via government data sharing and must be confirmed on the National Unified Electronic Tax Bureau; no separate paper VAT registration certificate is issued; (3) complete VAT taxpayer status formalities, with mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000; below that threshold, small-scale taxpayer status applies; (4) apply on the e-invoice platform for VAT invoice issuance rights, invoice allocation, and anti-counterfeit tax control initialization; (5) for a foreign non-resident entity without Chinese incorporation deriving China-source income, file non-resident enterprise tax registration with the competent STA office and obtain a non-resident taxpayer identification number using the home-country registration certificate and tax residence certificate
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under the Enterprise Income Tax Law; China does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity elections. Available status elections are limited to VAT small-scale versus general taxpayer filing status, and treaty relief for non-resident investors through the tax residence certificate process.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover threshold for tax registration itself; all WFOEs must register with the STA upon incorporation. The mandatory general VAT taxpayer threshold is RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales; small-scale taxpayers below that threshold may benefit from the current monthly VAT exemption of up to RMB 100,000 (RMB 300,000 per quarter) for ordinary taxable activities
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax System Phase IV electronic invoice platform. VAT invoices, including fully digital electronic invoices, must be issued through the STA e-invoice platform, are transmitted in real time to the tax authority, and carry a unified invoice classification code, serial number, digital e-signature, and anti-counterfeit QR stamp. Approved taxpayers may use API-based enterprise invoicing interfaces; Special VAT Invoices claimed for input VAT credit must be matched and verified in the electronic invoice system before credit is available.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods qualify for VAT zero-rating when physically exported from China under a valid GACC export declaration and sold to an offshore buyer. Cross-border services qualify only if supplied to a recipient outside China, wholly consumed outside China, and remunerated from outside China; the WFOE's 3D game-art outsourcing and character-rigging services may qualify as cross-border modern services under the VAT zero-rating/exemption rules for cross-border taxable activities if the offshore-consumption and payment-from-abroad tests are met. Zero-rating and export refund generally require general VAT taxpayer status and a properly filed export-service VAT rebate claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: GACC Electronic Export Customs Declaration (export goods customs declaration) evidencing physical departure from China
Original ocean Bill of Lading, airway bill, or international courier waybill evidencing export transportation
Commercial invoice and packing list exactly matching the export declaration
Export contract or purchase order with the offshore customer
Bank foreign-exchange receipt voucher / export proceeds settlement receipt issued by a designated foreign-exchange bank and recorded in the SAFE trade-in-goods monitoring system
For offshore services: signed cross-border service agreement, offshore recipient identity and address evidence, service acceptance or deliverable receipt, and offshore remittance record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax and customs authorities cross-match export declarations, transport documents, foreign-exchange receipts, and VAT rebate returns. Unverified or fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger clawback of the full refunded VAT, a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax, and an administrative fine of 100% to 500% of the refund fraudulently obtained under Article 66 of the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. Criminal liability may arise under Article 204 of the Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refund, and the taxpayer's compliance rating is downgraded, exposing prior periods to retrospective audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) and its State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) serve as the operative monetary and foreign-exchange authorities for the PRC-domiciled WFOE; Taiwan-side outward investment approval is also required from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange-rate regime with conditional current-account convertibility and controlled capital-account opening. Game 3D art outsourcing fees are current-account service-trade receipts: the WFOE may receive USD, TWD, or other convertible currencies in a designated FX settlement bank account, retain them, or sell them to the bank at the market rate after submitting the underlying service contract, invoice, and service-trade declaration to the bank. The capital account remains subject to SAFE and MOFCOM registration and approval: Taiwan-sourced equity must be injected through a SAFE-registered foreign-investment FX capital account and cannot be replaced by trade receivables or PayPal receipts. Dividend remittances are permissible but require audited financial statements, corporate income tax clearance, a board resolution, and a SAFE remittance declaration. The RMB is not freely transferable cross-border without an underlying real-economy transaction. Profit-stripping through misplaced royalties or transfer-pricing structures will be challenged by the bank. Banks must also verify the Taiwan investor's outbound investment approval from the relevant Taiwan competent authority as part of source-of-funds review. Overall, current-account proceeds are convertible, capital-account movements are strictly documented, and profit remittance is lawful only when all tax and SAFE requirements are cleared.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For the WFOE's service-trade exports, there is no statutory conversion ratio and no mandatory percentage of export proceeds to surrender. Export proceeds must be received by a licensed designated FX bank under SAFE total-amount verification and repatriated to China; bank monitoring expects collection within the contractually agreed payment term, normally 90 to 180 days from invoice date or service completion. If proceeds are not collected without a valid commercial or legal reason, the bank will escalate a suspicious transaction report. For goods-trade exports, proceeds must be repatriated within the period required by the goods-trade verification system, typically 180 days from customs declaration; however, this WFOE's 3D art outsourcing is service trade, so the bank applies the service-trade reporting code and contract-based verification rather than physical customs documents.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low. Offshore digital EMIs cannot legally provide the core settlement services required by a PRC WFOE because a foreign non-bank institution is not a SAFE-designated foreign-exchange bank and cannot open a RMB basic deposit account or an FDI FX capital account in China. EMIs such as international neobanks cannot accept compliant capital-account injections or dividend remittances on behalf of the mainland entity. PayPal may be used only as a low-value collection convenience and must be settled through the WFOE's licensed domestic bank; PayPal cannot process equity injection, profit repatriation, or other capital-account flows. Attempting to use any unlicensed EMI for capital movement will trigger AML refusal and regulatory rejection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory legal representatives of a WFOE must normally appear physically in-branch for first-time corporate account opening at a PRC bank, together with a second authorized signatory or financial controller. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted as a substitute for the physical branch visit. If the Taiwan-based legal representative cannot travel to mainland China, a notarized power of attorney may authorize a mainland-resident manager to appear, but the POA must be notarized in Taiwan, authenticated by the relevant Chinese consular or cross-strait trade office, and translated into English or Chinese where applicable; many banks will still require a live video interview with the legal representative and beneficial owners. Branch discretion remains the final determinant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwanese corporate shareholder with nominee shareholders and no audited financial statements makes the ultimate beneficial owner opaque.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a government-certified extract from the Taiwan company registry, articles of incorporation, and share register; audited financial statements or CPA-reviewed accounts for the latest two years; a signed UBO disclosure naming all natural persons with 25 percent or greater interest and all senior management; passport copies; notarized board resolution approving the WFOE incorporation and capital injection; and, if the Taiwan company is an investment-holding vehicle, evidence of its underlying business and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital is expected to arrive via a PayPal balance, a third-party wallet, or a third-country clearing account instead of the Taiwan shareholder's corporate bank account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Require the Taiwan investor to fund the equity injection from its own corporate bank account via SWIFT; provide bank statements showing the original PayPal or wallet balances being withdrawn to the corporate account; provide PayPal or platform business settlement reports; include an affidavit explaining the source of those balances; provide a written commitment that no equity injection will be routed through unlicensed money transmitters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Gaming-art outsourcing could be used to shift payments between affiliates, creating transfer-pricing and fake service risks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a full transfer-pricing local file if the related-party revenue threshold is met; supply executed master service agreements with explicit fee formulas, milestones, deliverables, and dispute mechanisms; provide per-project work orders, client acceptance emails, delivery receipts, and invoice schedules; maintain timesheets, payroll, and social-insurance records proving actual employees perform the art services; submit corporate income tax returns and CIT payment vouchers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE's registered address is a virtual office or the premises are still under preparation, causing the bank site inspection to fail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a good-standing lease agreement for a physical office in the WFOE's registered city, recent utility bills, photographs of the office interior, and an employer nameplate; if a serviced office is used, provide a sublicense agreement and landlord consent; present corporate seal custody logs and local employee contracts; cooperate fully with the bank's pre-onboarding site inspection and provide a business continuity plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before any funding, the WFOE must complete the foreign investment information reporting and obtain the SAFE FDI registration certificate. The bank opens the foreign-investment FX capital account after verifying the certificate and constitutional documents. The Taiwan parent then sends a SWIFT MT103 from its corporate bank account to the WFOE's FX capital account; the message must carry the direct-investment equity-capital purpose code and the FDI registration number in the remittance information. Upon receipt, the bank performs source-of-funds and capital verification; the funds are then settled into RMB only for approved operating purposes using supporting vouchers. PayPal, personal accounts, and transfers from third parties are unacceptable for equity injection. After receipt, the WFOE must complete capital-account closing verification within the applicable SAFE reporting timeframe and must not leave unverified funds stranded in transit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The WFOE receives client service fees in its FX settlement account or cross-border RMB account. Direct service payments should be completed via SWIFT MT103 with a service-trade purpose code; commercial LCs and documentary collections are permitted where end-clients require bank undertakings, but direct transfers are more practical for digital art delivery. For outbound payments to overseas contractors, the WFOE must submit the contract, invoice, and proof of service or delivery to the bank. For profit repatriation, the WFOE should first complete the annual audit and tax filing, then submit audited financial statements, tax clearance certificate, board resolution approving dividends, and a SAFE dividend remittance application; the bank converts RMB and remits via SWIFT MT103 under the investment-income purpose code. Cross-border RMB may also clear through CIPS where the counterparty agrees, but SWIFT remains the default for Taiwan-mainland flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/FX forward contracts with a genuine trade or capital exposure, executed through a licensed designated bank
Cross-currency swaps for long-term FDI-related FX exposures, subject to SAFE and PRC banking approval and actual principal-service cash flows
FX swaps to control refinancing or cash-flow timing mismatches on current-account and capital-account transactions
Purchased plain-vanilla FX options used solely for hedging, with no naked option writing by the client
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible in the onshore RMB market; the WFOE must use deliverable forwards only and cannot settle NDFs against RMB exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements comprising balance sheet, profit and loss statement, changes in equity, and cash flow statement, together with directors report and employees and directors remuneration report, prepared and submitted for approval at the ordinary shareholders meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors and shareholders meeting, with subsequent oversight by the Ministry of Economic Affairs Commercial Registration Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 June of the year following each calendar financial year, being six months after the 31 December fiscal year end; if the company has an approved non-calendar fiscal year, the meeting must be held within six months of that year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the ordinary shareholders meeting within six months of the financial year end allows the central competent authority to impose administrative fines of TWD 10,000 to TWD 500,000 per event and to order remedial convocation; continued non-compliance is an administrative dissolution and strike-off trigger under the Taiwan Company Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved financial statements, detailed profit and loss statement, profit distribution or loss absorption proposal, and minutes of the ordinary shareholders meeting filed for registration with the central competent authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Commercial Registration Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days after the shareholders meeting approval, and in any event by no later than 15 July for a calendar-year company if the meeting is held at the statutory deadline of 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts administrative fines of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000 per violation under Company Act Article 387; the MOEA may order rectification for each consecutive year of default, and repeated refusal to file is a ground for administrative dissolution and removal from the corporate register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return, including the audited or CPA-attested financial statements when the statutory threshold is met, foreign related-party disclosure schedules, and any retained-earnings surtax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau of the region in which the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the year following the prior calendar financial year; the effective filing season is 1 May through 31 May, and the return covers the preceding 1 January to 31 December period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent tax accrues simple interest at the one-year postal savings fixed deposit rate from the original due date until payment; late payment also incurs a surcharge of 1 percent of the unpaid tax for every two days of delay up to a maximum of 15 percent; underpayment or non-filing after official notification may trigger a penalty of up to three times the understated tax liability and compulsory tax enforcement against bank accounts and assets, with persistent non-compliance exposing the company to revocation of business registration and administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bimonthly value-added business tax return for the previous two-month filing period, with zero-rated export invoices and input tax deductions on game-art outsourcing expenses, and any corresponding VAT payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau of the region in which the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the second month following each two-month period; for a calendar-year company the deadlines recur as 15 March, 15 May, 15 July, 15 September, 15 November, and 15 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment of business tax is subject to a surcharge of 1 percent of the unpaid tax for each two-day delay up to 15 percent, plus interest at the one-year postal savings deposit rate; a delinquent return under deemed assessment can attract a penalty of up to three times the unpaid tax, and habitual non-filing may lead to forced seizure of assets, revocation of the business registration, and administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual company information and ultimate beneficial ownership confirmation, updating the director, supervisor, manager, and 10-percent-or-more shareholder data on the Company Information Platform and confirming the statutory registers against the share register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Information Platform and Commercial Registration Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days of any change in directors, supervisors, managers, or shareholders holding at least 10 percent of the issued shares; if no change occurs, an annual year-end confirmation should be completed no later than 31 December of the reporting year and filed immediately after the ordinary shareholders meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the Company Act Article 22-1 filing obligation exposes the company and its responsible officer to administrative fines of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000 per violation; making a false UBO registry entry can trigger criminal liability under AML-related provisions, and repeated non-compliance is an administrative dissolution and strike-off trigger before the central competent authority

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan private WFOE is legally required to obtain an independent CPA audit where any of the following quantitative triggers is met: (i) balance-sheet paid-in capital reaches or exceeds TWD 30,000,000, approximately USD 950,000, regardless of revenue or headcount, under Company Act Article 20 and the MOEA rules on CPA certification of company financial statements; (ii) annual operating turnover or taxable revenue reaches or exceeds TWD 100,000,000, approximately USD 3,100,000, in which case the annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return must be accompanied by a CPA-attested financial report; (iii) the company qualifies as a public issuer or is regulated by the Financial Supervisory Commission under the Securities and Exchange Act, in which case annual financial statements must be audited by a CPA and semi-annual financial statements reviewed by a CPA; and (iv) the tax authority or MOEA formally issued an administrative demand for CPA certification based on business complexity or foreign-investment reporting requirements. There is no standalone headcount audit trigger for a Taiwan private company; headcount data affects labor, health insurance, and pension filings but does not itself compel an independent audit. The target WFOE engaged in 3D game-art outsourcing and below these thresholds will not be subject to a mandatory statutory audit in a standard operating year, although the corporate secretary should re-test the thresholds before each 30 June shareholders meeting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with the Taiwan Business Entity Accounting Act and the applicable accounting standards approved by the Financial Supervisory Commission and the Accounting Research and Development Foundation; public and FSC-regulated enterprises apply Taiwan-IFRS, while non-public small and medium WFOEs may apply the Enterprise Accounting Standards, which are local GAAP substantially aligned with IFRS for SMEs; tax-return figures are derived from these financial statements and then adjusted for permanent and temporary differences under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not operate a stand-alone annual UBO return or a 30-day reporting window; instead, under Company Act Article 22-1, every non-public company must maintain and file on the MOEA Company Information Platform the identity of directors, supervisors, managers, and all shareholders holding 10 percent or more of the issued shares, and must update that platform within 15 calendar days of any share transfer or appointment change that alters the disclosed data. For annual secretarial maintenance, the corporate secretary must perform a register audit before the ordinary shareholders meeting, reconcile the on-site share register, register of directors, charges, and minute book against the MOEA platform record, obtain updated beneficial-ownership declarations from each 10-percent-or-more shareholder, and include a management representation in the board minutes confirming that no undisclosed beneficial owner or unregistered share transfer occurred during the previous 12 months; any change discovered must be filed on the platform within the remaining 15-day statutory window, with no 30-day grace period available.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 to USD 1,500 per year for a compliant Taiwan registered office and corporate service agent arrangement, exclusive of physical office lease costs in Taipei or city-center locations
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to USD 15,000 for a small or medium private WFOE where a certified CPA audit is legally triggered; USD 2,500 to USD 6,000 for a non-statutory financial statement compilation or agreed-upon procedures engagement in non-audit years

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard enterprise income tax rate under PRC EIT Law Article 4; reduced to 15% for qualified High/New-Technology Enterprises and to 5% effective rate for small low-profit enterprises within statutory thresholds
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprise preference: annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, employee count not exceeding 300, and total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million qualify for an effective CIT rate of 5% (2023-2027). R&D expenses qualify for 100% super deduction on eligible qualifying R&D expenditures. Certain regional incentives such as Hainan Free Trade Port and Shanghai Lingang may grant a 15% rate for qualifying encouraged industries. No automatic free-zone or patent box exemption applies to a 3D game-art outsourcing studio unless it independently meets the High/New-Technology Enterprise criteria through genuine and documented R&D activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (China Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return A-Class), filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal (China Electronic Tax Administration) or in person at the competent Chinese tax authority with jurisdiction over the WFOE's registered address.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional estimated tax payments using the quarterly A200000 return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and final tax payment must be filed and settled within 5 months after the end of the tax year, i.e., by May 31 of the following calendar year. Quarterly provisional returns and advance CIT payments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Filing Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax ID, registered address, industrial classification (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541430), legal representative, accounting system, and tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise under EIT Law Article 2 because it is incorporated in China and its place of effective management is in China. The Taiwan parent must not be identified as the taxpayer on this return; list the Taiwan parent only if it has a permanent establishment in China requiring separate registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from AAA game asset 3D sculpting, character rigging, texturing, model creation, and related art outsourcing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert Taiwan-dollar or other foreign-currency receipts to RMB using the spot exchange rate prevailing on the date of income recognition. Intercompany revenue from the Taiwan parent or affiliated group must reflect the arm's length price; if the Taiwan parent pays for services, ensure the WFOE actually renders the service, retains risk, and earns a functional profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct and indirect costs: artists' payroll, software licensing, workstation depreciation, office rent, subcontracting charges, travel, communication, and other ordinary and necessary business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to Taiwan group companies must be supported by contracts, invoices, proof of actual service receipt, and evidence that fees are not disguised profit distributions. Excessive related-party interest is subject to thin-capitalization limits of 2:1 debt-to-equity for non-financial enterprises; payments to Taiwan without withholding constitute a violation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes total accounting profit before tax based on PRC Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that profit is not artificially reduced by charging excessive management fees or royalties to the Taiwan parent. If the WFOE receives funds from Taiwan for services actually performed in China, the income must be fully included; no deduction is allowed for deemed dividends or equity distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs for non-deductible expenditures (e.g., tax penalties, excess entertainment and advertising expenses, non-business expenses) and deductions for tax-exempt income, additional R&D deductions, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to Taiwan for royalties, interest, or services must be separately examined for substance and withholding documentation. If the Taiwan parent is a mere passive investor, its intercompany charges may be recharacterized as constructive dividends subject to 10% withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Loss Carryforward and Net Operating Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct prior-year losses within the statutory carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE's unabsorbed losses cannot be transferred to or deducted by the Taiwan parent. Losses are capped at 5 years for general enterprises and 10 years for qualified High/New-Technology Enterprises. A Taiwan parent cannot claim a tax deduction for the WFOE's losses in Taiwan unless permitted by Taiwan domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Taxable Income and Applicable Tax Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the standard 25% rate to taxable income, before preferences and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE qualifies as a small low-profit enterprise, the effective rate is 5% on taxable income up to RMB 3 million; if the WFOE misrepresents employee count or assets to obtain this preference, the tax authority will impose penalties and the entity may lose the preferential rate. Non-resident shareholders should not include their own deductions or losses on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Tax Payable, Credits, and Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute tax payable, then apply foreign tax credits, domestic tax credits that are available, and quarterly prepayments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any Taiwan income taxes actually paid on foreign-source income of the WFOE may be creditable under PRC foreign tax credit rules, subject to the foreign tax credit limitation. However, withholding taxes borne by the Taiwan shareholder on dividends distributed by the WFOE are not creditable against the WFOE's own CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Final Tax Due or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determines the balance of tax due or overpayment refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The final tax due must be paid by May 31. Any underpayment will attract daily late interest of 0.05% per day; any overpayment may be offset or refunded upon application. The declaration of a dividend does not create a deductible expense and does not reduce the final tax due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of the legal representative, financial officer, and tax preparer, with company seal and date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan parent should not sign the Chinese CIT return unless it has registered a permanent establishment in China. The legal representative and financial officer personally certify the truthfulness of the return; false certification may trigger personal liability and criminal exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under the Tax Collection Administration Law: if the return is not filed within the prescribed period, the tax authority may impose a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; for a serious violation, RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. Understatement or non-payment due to fraudulent conduct constitutes tax evasion under TCAL Article 63, punishable by a fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. If the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and accounts for more than 10% of the taxable amount, criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 may subject the person-in-charge to imprisonment of up to 7 years plus fines. The WFOE may also be listed as a 'seriously untrustworthy taxpayer', triggering restrictions on credit, procurement, and exit from China for its legal representative.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form F500000 (Withholding Enterprise Income Tax Return for Non-resident Enterprises, or Kohji Soyoku 扣缴企业所得税报告表) filed by the WFOE as a withholding agent through the China Electronic Tax Administration portal, plus the corresponding bank tax payment voucher.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Event-driven: a separate return must be filed at the time of each withholding obligation arising from outbound dividend, interest, or royalty payments to the Taiwan parent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax withheld must be turned over to the State Tax Administration within 7 days after the withholding obligation arises. For dividends, the obligation arises on the date of the shareholders' resolution declaring the dividend or on the date of actual payment, whichever is earlier. For interest and royalties, the obligation arises on the date the income is paid or deemed paid under Chinese tax law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name, address, foreign tax identification number, country/jurisdiction of residence, and tax residency status of the Taiwan parent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a certified Tax Residency Certificate from the Taiwan tax authority if treaty relief is claimed under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement; because that Agreement has not entered into force, statutory 10% withholding currently applies. If the Taiwan parent asserts that it is not tax resident in Taiwan, obtain and retain evidence; the WFOE remains liable for the correctness of the withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Specify the income type: 2a dividends; 2b interest; 2c royalties; 2d business profits / services; 2e other.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Outbound dividends from a Chinese resident enterprise are always 'dividend income' for withholding purposes, regardless of the Taiwan entity's accounting treatment. Payments for game-art licensing, trademarks, or copyrighted software from the Taiwan parent are 'royalties'; payments for actual services, if the Taiwan parent has no China PE, are business profits not subject to CIT withholding, but may be recharacterized if substance is lacking.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The gross amount of income paid or payable to the Taiwan parent, expressed in RMB after currency conversion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For dividends, use the total declared distribution; no deduction for Chinese taxes is allowed. For interest and royalties, the gross amount includes any withholding tax borne by the payer if the contract is silent or states 'net amount', requiring grossing-up to compute taxable income. For royalties, value-added tax is imposed separately at 6% on the service import, with the VAT collected by the withholding agent together with CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The CIT withholding rate applied to the gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The statutory rate for dividends, interest, and royalties paid to a non-resident enterprise is 10% under EIT Law. No treaty reduction is currently available for Taiwan because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement is not yet effective; therefore the rate must be 10%, not 5% or 7%. If the Taiwan parent has a permanent establishment in China and the income is effectively connected to that PE, Box 4 would be inapplicable and the PE would file Form A100000 instead.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the amount of tax withheld: gross taxable amount x applicable rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax must be withheld at the later of the date of payment or the date the income is recognized; for dividends, withholding cannot be deferred by delaying the bank remittance after the shareholder resolution is passed. The withheld amount must be paid into the state treasury within 7 days, and the payment voucher number must be recorded on the F500000 return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of whether the withholding rate is reduced by a bilateral agreement, with attachments (Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial owner declaration, shareholding certification).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For current Taiwan-related payments, the 'no treaty' box should be ticked. To preserve the right to claim a refund if the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement eventually becomes effective, the WFOE should retain the Taiwan parent's Tax Residency Certificate, board minutes of the Taiwan parent, organizational chart, and evidence that the Taiwan parent has beneficial ownership and substantive economic existence. Claiming treaty relief without a valid TRC exposes the WFOE to penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature and seal of the legal representative and financial controller of the WFOE, confirming the accuracy of the information and timely payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The legal representative of the WFOE is the responsible person for withholding compliance. Signing a false declaration that the Taiwan parent qualifies for treaty relief when it does not may lead to personal criminal liability for assisting in tax evasion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: If the WFOE fails to withhold, the tax authority under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 69 may assess a fine of 50% to 300% of the unpaid tax and order the WFOE to remit the tax. Late remittance of the withheld tax accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05%. Willful failure to remit withheld taxes that were collected may be treated as criminal embezzlement of tax funds under Criminal Law Article 404, exposing the legal representative and financial officer to imprisonment of up to 10 years in aggravated cases. Additionally, each F500000 late filing attracts a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, and the company may be put on the tax credit blacklist.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax under PRC EIT Law on dividends paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise; no reduced treaty rate is currently available for Taiwan because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement (the 'Cross-Strait Tax Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Enhancement of Tax Cooperation') was signed in 2015 but has not entered into force.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because no effective bilateral double tax treaty exists between China and Taiwan at the time of filing, treaty relief cannot be invoked. If and when the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement enters into force, the WFOE as withholding agent must: (1) obtain a current-year Tax Residency Certificate for the Taiwan beneficial owner issued by the Taiwan tax authority; (2) obtain a completed and signed Beneficial Ownership Declaration confirming the Taiwan parent is the ultimate economic owner and is not a pass-through or conduit; (3) substantiate the Taiwan parent's direct shareholding in the WFOE at the threshold required for the reduced dividend rate; (4) file the Non-resident Enterprise Reduced Withholding Tax Rate Application with the competent tax authority before or at the time of distribution; (5) attach board resolutions, share registers, and audited financial statements evidencing active economic substance and no abuse of the agreement; (6) remit the remaining tax within 7 days and keep all supporting documents for at least 10 years. Absent such rigorous documentation, the full 10% statutory rate applies and the WFOE must not unilaterally apply a lower rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound interest and royalties paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise is 10% EIT; royalties additionally attract value-added tax at 6% on the service import, with the VAT withheld and remitted jointly. No treaty-reduced rate for Taiwan is currently available. If the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement becomes effective, the negotiated source rates are expected to be 5% for dividends paid to a beneficial owner holding at least 25% of the capital, 10% for other dividends, and 7% for interest and royalties; however, these rates are not enforceable until the agreement's entry-into-force instrument is completed and published.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under SAT Bulletin 2016 No.42, a contemporaneous Local File is mandatory for a resident enterprise whose related-party transactions in the prior year exceed: (i) RMB 200 million for purchase/sale of tangible goods; (ii) RMB 100 million for transfer/licensing of intangible property; (iii) RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers; (iv) RMB 40 million for provision/rendering of services. A Master File is required when the aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion. The WFOE, even at a lower turnover, must prepare a Transfer Pricing Contemporaneous File if any service threshold is crossed; the file must be completed by May 31 of the following year and submitted within 30 days upon the tax authority's request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not maintain an explicit UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation statute, but the 'substance over form' doctrine, PRC General Anti-Avoidance Rule under EIT Law Articles 47-48, and tax treaty 'beneficial ownership' principles require the WFOE to demonstrate real economic substance. The WFOE must have a physical office, full-time 3D artists and riggers, actual control over core production decisions, and genuine risk-bearing capability. Core Income-Generating Activities ('CIGA') for game-art outsourcing include concept finalization, 3D sculpting, texture creation, rigging, quality assurance, project management, and invoicing; these activities must be performed in China by the WFOE, not merely by a Taiwan parent. If the Taiwan parent controls the economic substance while the WFOE functions as a mere booking vehicle, the tax authority can recharacterize income, disallow deductions, and impose special tax adjustment interest at 5 percentage points above the benchmark on the underpaid tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Document Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE repeatedly sells 3D art services to the Taiwan parent at a price yielding a 2% net margin while comparable independent art studios yield 15%, and fabricates contracts, invoices, and timesheets to cover the mispricing, causing the Chinese taxable income to be understated by more than RMB 500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41 and 47, Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63 (tax evasion), and SAT Special Tax Adjustment Measures: the tax authority may reallocate income, impose an additional 0.05% daily late surcharge, and assess a penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. Criminal Law Article 201 provides for imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines when the evaded tax is relatively large and constitutes more than 10% of the tax payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced under PRC Company Law Article 20 when the director abusively uses the limited liability entity to evade tax and prejudice creditors. Directors are personally liable for civil restitution of misappropriated assets, their personal bank accounts can be frozen, they are subject to exit bans and travel blacklisting ('seriously untrustworthy taxpayer' list), and they face criminal imprisonment for tax evasion for up to 7 years; financial officers who knowingly prepare false documentation are treated as accomplices.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Administration - Failure to Withhold and Remit Dividend WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE passes a shareholder resolution declaring a RMB 10 million dividend to the Taiwan parent and wires the full amount without withholding the 10% non-resident enterprise income tax, and does not file Form F500000 within the 7-day statutory period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Administration Law Article 69: the withdrawal agent must be fined 50% to 300% of the tax that should have been withheld; the tax remains collectible from the withholding agent together with daily late surcharge at 0.05%; the competent tax authority may also issue a rectification notice requiring payment within 15 days. If the company wilfully disposes of assets to avoid collection, the persons in charge may be criminally prosecuted under Criminal Law Article 203 for tax evasion and obstruction of collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and financial controller who directed the non-withholding can be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid withheld tax to the extent the company's assets are insufficient; the tax authority may list the directors in the exit-control database, allowing border police to prevent departure from China. Directors may face administrative detention for refusal to comply and criminal fines; if the withheld sums were diverted to personal use, imprisonment of up to 10 years for misappropriation or embezzlement is possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance (GAAR and AML Risk)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is registered in a Chinese city offering tax incentives but has no physical office, no full-time employees, and no genuine game-art production activity; the Taiwan parent retains all negotiating power and operational control, and the WFOE merely receives payments and re-invoices them to Taiwan while claiming the small low-profit 5% CIT rate and R&D super deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 47 (General Anti-Avoidance Rule) and Article 48 allow the tax authority to recharacterize the entire scheme, deny the incentives, adjust the taxable income, and impose special tax adjustment interest increased by 5 percentage points. If fraudulent, TCAL Article 63 applies with a 50%-500% penalty; the Anti-Money Laundering Law and Criminal Law Article 191 also impose fines and confiscation on shell companies involved in the laundering of illegal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who commingle personal assets with the shell company's funds can be personally liable for the company's debts under Company Law Article 20. They face civil asset restitution orders, permanent blacklisting from serving as directors in China, travel bans, and criminal liability for tax fraud or money laundering with imprisonment of up to 10 years in aggravated cases; where illegal proceeds exceed RMB 10 million, administrative fines of up to RMB 5 million may b e imposed personally.
